messages.author: 6dd9bc4fd62b481b
messages.subject: Interpreting cross validation graph results
parts:
Hi all, 
Fairly new to using DAPC in local scale pop genetics. I performed DAPC on my ddRADseq data set and after running the cross validation component I got a seemingly nice Root Mean Squared Error by Number of PCs of PCA (0.1807392 for 25 PCs). However the graph results are confusing and I am concerned I may be over fitting....
Any advice is greatly appreciated.

Attached is the Cross validation graph produced by xvalDapc. 

We plan to include additional supplementary individuals to further validate our model.

Nathan

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Interpreting cross validation graph results
parts:
Hi Nathan,

This is a strange pattern indeed. I will preface this that DAPC is an adegenet-specific issue and this question really belongs on the adegenet forum.

It's hard for me to know what parameters you set or what your data look like, so I'm just going to tell you what I can only assume based on this graph.

The cross-validation procedure by default works by leaving out 10% from each population, calculating DAPC, predicting where those 10% belong, and repeating this 100 or so times. Given the regular spacing for these points, I would suspect that you might have small sample sizes for your populations. This also might be due to the fact that restriction-based methods generate a lot of missing data, but DAPC forces missing values to be the mean of the data, so you might have some issues with non-random missingness.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

Nathan

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Interpreting cross validation graph results
parts:
I don’t think it can hurt to remove loci for this since the loci containing the signal of population structure will have a strong influence on the principle components. It is also important to be aware that sample size really is the limiting factor for DAPC. In addition, I would highly recommend reading the adegenet tutorial on DAPC if you haven’t already. 

Sent from my iPhone
